presentation.label: MORPHA
presentation.summary: A wavetable synth machine: it sweeps through a table of waves, from your own sample or a built-in one, bending each wave as it plays.
presentation.overview: Morpha is a new machine in the track's machine list. It reads a wavetable, a row of single waves, and plays one of them as an oscillator at the note's pitch: POS picks the place in the table and Morpha morphs smoothly between the two waves around it, so turning POS or modulating it with an LFO changes the tone as it plays. The table is the track's sample (a wavetable file of 2,048-sample waves morphs wave by wave; any other sample is scanned smoothly from end to end), or, with no sample, a built-in table of 48 waves that runs from sine through triangle, saw, square and pulse to two vowel-like waves. WARP bends each wave four ways (BEND, SYNC, MIRR, FOLD) by AMT, DETN thickens it with two detuned copies, and MIX blends in a sine an octave below. The Digitakt's own filter, amp envelope, LFOs and effects shape it like any machine. For chords, link tracks as voices in SETTINGS (VOICES), a feature of the Digitakt II base.
highlights: Its own machine in the track's machine list, saved with the kit.
Plays your own wavetables, or a built-in table with no sample at all.
Four warp modes and three-oscillator unison.
Polyphonic through the base's linked voices: each note of a chord on its own track.
usage: Choose Morpha with no sample and slowly sweep POS with an LFO for a tone that keeps changing.
Load a wavetable file as a sample, set WARP to SYNC and lock AMT on some trigs for movement.
Turn DETN up and link three tracks as voices for wide pads and chords.

access.location: The machine list of a track (FUNC + SRC), after the stock machines.
steps: Hold FUNC and press SRC to open the machine list.
Scroll down past the stock machines to MORPHA and press YES.
Choose a wavetable sample with knob D on the SRC page, or none for the built-in table.

controls.name: TUNE (knob A)
controls.doc: The pitch, as SAMPLE's TUNE. A note at the track's default pitch plays middle C.

controls.name: WARP (knob B)
controls.doc: How the wave is bent: BEND pushes it towards its ends, SYNC restarts it up to four times a cycle, MIRR plays it forward then back, FOLD folds its level back on itself.

controls.name: AMT (knob C)
controls.doc: How much WARP bends the wave; at 0 the wave plays as it is.

controls.name: SAMP (knob D)
controls.doc: The wavetable: a wavetable file of 2,048-sample waves, any other sample (scanned), or none for the built-in table.

controls.name: POS (knob E)
controls.doc: Which wave of the table plays, morphing smoothly between neighbouring waves.

controls.name: MIX (knob F)
controls.doc: The wave against a sine one octave below: full the wave alone, the middle both, 0 the sine alone.

controls.name: DETN (knob G)
controls.doc: Unison: one oscillator at 0; turned up, two more detuned up and down by up to half a semitone.

limitations: Needs the Digitakt II base with added machines and its full-resolution knobs C and E; polyphony needs the base's linked voices.
Waves are read without band-limiting: very bright waves played high can alias.

load.display: About 2% of the sound chip per sounding note with every knob up (emulator)
load.conditions: One note, DETN up (three oscillators), MIX in the middle, AMT and POS up: up to 14,977 emulator instructions per block of 666,667; a stock SAMPLE note about 7,000. A unit's cycle count is not measured.
